item.title: Implement ledger.py per SPEC.md with focused tests
item.brief:
Operator request (verbatim): "Implement `ledger.py` according to `SPEC.md`. Preserve the documented API, handle every specified error and boundary case, and add focused tests. The existing tests cover basics only. Use the Python standard library and commit your work."

Read SPEC.md in the repository root first; it is the authority for the API, errors and boundary cases. Implement every behaviour it specifies in ledger.py, keeping the documented API unchanged. Extend test_ledger.py (or add focused tests alongside it) to cover each specified error and boundary case, not only the basics. Use only the Python standard library. Run the test suite and make sure it passes before finishing. Commit the work on the item's branch with a clear message; no attribution lines beyond the required Co-Authored-By line.

pr.body: Approach: ledger.py holds a copy of the balances behind one threading.Lock. transfer() validates the amount, then looks up both accounts (KeyError if unknown), then checks funds and destination overflow before writing both sides under the lock. snapshot() returns a copy under the same lock. Key files: ledger.py, test_ledger.py. Checks: python3 -B -m unittest test_ledger, 34 tests OK, three runs. Assumptions: built-in int means type(x) is int; names must be str instances. Limits: bare asserts are stripped under python -O; the concurrency tests are probabilistic at detecting races.
pr.summary: Made Ledger work per SPEC.md. Now validates inputs, rejects bad balances, names and amounts, and makes transfers atomic under one lock. Before: NotImplementedError stubs. Now: 34 passing tests covering every specified error and boundary case, plus concurrency tests.
